channel.title: Pier & Point · Mission Rock Block J
channel.description: Changes, corrections and dated milestones for Mission Rock Block J (Mission Rock), San Francisco. Every item names its source.

item.title: Correction · Mission Rock Block J: Corrections to Block J: the Design Controls are now called a document dated April 24, 2018. The base-building height fact now gives 60 ft with a 40 ft maximum along the Terry A. Francois Boulevard side, not 40 ft alone. The phase-status fact no longer presents the 2023 deceleration as the current state; it adds the June 2026 request to accelerate Phase 2. The Design Controls approval milestone now cites the Sept 2019 Port memo that gives the Jan 30, 2018 date and notes the memo numbers that resolution 18-05 while the January 26 staff report requested it as 18-04. The Board of Supervisors milestone no longer names 'Resolution 33-18' (the Port's reports call it a resolution and an ordinance; the Notice of Determination gives File No. 171286). The Oct 2023 milestone now says Port and developer staff agreed earlier in 2023 to decelerate Phase 2 and that Resolution 23-46's recitals state it, rather than a Commission finding on Oct 10; the March 2025 milestone quotes the memo's words and calls the 132 BMR-unit cut a proposal. The Draft EIR phasing milestone no longer says it was 'superseded'; it cites the Port's Oct 2023 list of Phase 1 buildings. The D4D source is retitled the March 2012 Design + Development Revised Proposal by the Giants and The Cordish Companies (a developer proposal, not the Design for Development), the Design Controls source is credited to the Port only, and the Design Controls figure credit no longer names Mission Rock Partners or an adoption date. The map notes now say no source read shows construction on the block and cite the Port's June 2026 report instead of a bare 'unbuilt'; the 'within 3%' area claim is corrected in a new dated note (lot A is about 3.3% under the 2012 table).

item.title: Milestone · Mission Rock Block J: Port staff's memo for the Commission's March 11, 2025 meeting (Item 12A, Resolution 25-17) proposes cutting Phase 1's BMR units from 161 to 132 and says later phases 'may require higher percentages of BMR units' to meet the project's 40% overall target; the Developer, Port and MOHCD are reviewing changes 'with the goal of improving the feasibility of future Phases of Mission Rock' (Mar 11, 2025)

item.title: Planned · Mission Rock Block J: Port Commission adopts Resolution 23-46 (October 10, 2023); its recitals state that, because Phase 2 is 'not currently financially feasible', Port and Developer staff had 'mutually agreed earlier this year to decelerate work on Phase 2' (Oct 10, 2023)
